title: NavigateFlow: Consolidated Dashboard, Rollout & Cost Navigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We will redesign the Console navigation to present dashboards, rollout controls, and cost views as a coherent, discoverable flow. Current feedback shows users struggle to find per-route cost breakdowns and to switch between rollout variants while monitoring KPIs. This ticket captures the primary prototype, rationale, and test outcomes for a compact, context-aware left rail and a transient workspace switcher that preserves task state.
context: Redwood Console currently has fragmentation between Observability (dashboards), Rollouts (canary/A-B), and Billing (cost breakdowns). Teams frequently open multiple tabs or lose context when switching workspaces. This causes slower troubleshooting and rollout rollbacks. The redesign aims to reduce time-to-insight and reduce accidental config changes during rollouts.
goals: Make per-route cost and latency metrics one click from a rollout action
Reduce workspace-switch-induced task churn by preserving active route and filters
Provide a compact left navigation that surfaces rollouts, dashboards, and cost without adding cognitive load
scope: In scope: left rail IA updates, compact workspace switcher prototype, rollout toolbar with metric peek, cost-summary flyout, routing semantics for saved filters
Out of scope: backend billing model changes, dedicated capacity pricing model, full telemetry rewrite
usability_findings: Early testing (n=7 engineers) — +42% faster to locate per-route cost compared to baseline
Users liked inline rollout metric peek but wanted quick 'jump to traces' link
Some confusion around ephemeral vs. pinned workspaces; added microcopy to clarify
decisions: Adopt compact left rail with three primary clusters: Observability, Rollouts, Cost; secondary items collapsed
Workspace switcher becomes a modal overlay that preserves active route context by default
Introduce 'metric peek' affordance on rollout items that surfaces the last 24h cost and p50/p95 latency
tradeoffs: Compact rail reduces visual scanning but increases depth for less-used routes
Preserving route state across workspace switchers increases client-side complexity and may require migration in routing logic
Metric peek fetches additional telemetry data on hover which could increase API load if not cached
acceptance_criteria: 1) Left rail flows implemented in prototype and validated by product/eng; 2) Workspace switcher preserves route/filter state in 90% of test cases; 3) Metric peek shows correct last-24h cost and latency for selected route; 4) No regressions in console keyboard navigation
next_steps: Address engineering feedback about client-side routing complexity (ENG sync scheduled 2026-03-15)
Implement lightweight server-side cache for metric peek (ENG-3729)
Run second usability round with two production customers (PM to coordinate)
Create implementation tickets for rollout toolbar and cost flyout
notes: 2026-03-02: Design review — PM requested clearer separation between customer-level and org-level cost metrics
2026-03-05: Engineering review — suggested client-side router checkpointing to preserve filters across switches
2026-03-10: Usability synthesis — added microcopy and single-click 'open in new tab' affordance for advanced users
